account: Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) made Wajiro and the other Kashii Line stations except Kashii and Chōjabaru unstaffed from 14 March 2015 and serves their passengers remotely. OPTiM Corporation announced on 6 October 2017 a demonstration trial of its “AI Physical Security Service” from 10 October 2017. It would run at two JR Kyushu stations: 和白駅 (Wajiro) on the Kashii Line and 二島駅 (Futajima) on the Chikuho Main Line. The service, on “OPTiM Cloud IoT OS”, has AI monitor network-camera video in real time. When it detects an anomaly, it shows an alert and emails administrators. OPTiM says that this is to reduce the burden on operators who watch many monitors and to raise safety in the station. The release includes an image of station camera analysis identifying people, trains and the yellow platform line. OPTiM published the release on optim.co.jp, and @Press republished it. The release is the only source on the JR Kyushu trial. JR Kyushu is not quoted. The release gives no trial end date and no list of detection targets. No result of the JR Kyushu trial has been published. The only reported detection rate, 96.2% against a 90% target, comes from OPTiM's later trial at JR East's Sawa station, announced on 26 June 2018. Station romanizations are ours.

ai_role.statement: The vendor describes the AI's intended part as real-time video monitoring with alerts on the monitor and by email to administrators, to ease the load on operators who watch many monitors. No source reports what the AI detected at Wajiro or Futajima or how staff responded, and JR Kyushu has published no account of the trial.

fields.account: Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) made Wajiro and the other Kashii Line stations except Kashii and Chōjabaru unstaffed from 14 March 2015 and serves their passengers remotely. OPTiM Corporation announced on 6 October 2017 a demonstration trial of its “AI Physical Security Service” from 10 October 2017. It would run at two JR Kyushu stations: 和白駅 (Wajiro) on the Kashii Line and 二島駅 (Futajima) on the Chikuho Main Line. The service, on “OPTiM Cloud IoT OS”, has AI monitor network-camera video in real time. When it detects an anomaly, it shows an alert and emails administrators. OPTiM says that this is to reduce the burden on operators who watch many monitors and to raise safety in the station. The release includes an image of station camera analysis identifying people, trains and the yellow platform line. OPTiM published the release on optim.co.jp, and @Press republished it. The release is the only source on the JR Kyushu trial. JR Kyushu is not quoted. The release gives no trial end date and no list of detection targets. No result of the JR Kyushu trial has been published. The only reported detection rate, 96.2% against a 90% target, comes from OPTiM's later trial at JR East's Sawa station, announced on 26 June 2018. Station romanizations are ours.
